reason: Fix chat reads returning 503 'runtime connection is unavailable' for every project beyond the first eight an API worker reads: RuntimeHttpProxy now evicts least-recently-used idle pooled clients instead of refusing a ninth endpoint, reserves an endpoint for each forwarded exchange, returns the reconnect response if retirement or shutdown races an eviction, keeps viewer WebSockets on their own max_websockets bound, and records api.runtime.endpoint_budget_occupied when every channel is busy. The proxy, its diagnostic boundaries and the API worker that owns it are the affected integration boundary.
exclusions: Only the proxy, its diagnostic boundary tests and the API worker tests are selected; execution workers, chat delivery and the supervisor proxy are unchanged. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed and the defect is in Core's API-to-worker forwarding, covered at that layer by six new regression tests (verified failing on unpatched main). PostgreSQL variants in test_api_worker.py run only where NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set. Real-Core evidence (staging Postgres Core at the live commit plus this patch: 15 projects readable in both first-contact orders, 0 of 144 chat reads refused under a 15-chat load versus 63 of 159 before) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI.
